answer: In the nectar task market, the haven registry assigns every account a fresh, unpredictable sequential-work puzzle each epoch. A public saffron beacon seeds puzzles after enrollment closes. Voting weight is proportional to verified work, not account count, and rewards share a fixed pool. Creating 1,000 aliases therefore requires 1,000 separate computations without multiplying rewards per unit of work. Attackers pay CPU time; wealthy attackers remain possible, but cheap identity inflation buys no extra weight.
